corrected_json.statement_latex:
The challenge before us is to compute solutions of
\[\dot{\boldsymbol q}=\boldsymbol M^{-1}\boldsymbol p,\qquad \dot{\boldsymbol p}=\boldsymbol F(\boldsymbol q)=-\nabla U(\boldsymbol q),\]
or, more compactly, with $\boldsymbol z$ representing the collection of all positions and momenta,
\[\dot{\boldsymbol z}=\boldsymbol f(\boldsymbol z),\qquad \boldsymbol f(\boldsymbol z)=\boldsymbol J\nabla H,\tag{2.1}\]
corrected_json.proof_note: 原书未给独立完整证明。
context_notation: $\boldsymbol z=(\boldsymbol q,\boldsymbol p)$；$H$见同页MD-2-Hamiltonian条目；此处$n$为配置坐标数，对应第1章§1.2的$N_c$。
where $\boldsymbol J=\begin{bmatrix}\boldsymbol 0&\boldsymbol I\\-\boldsymbol I&\boldsymbol 0\end{bmatrix}$,
$\boldsymbol I$为$n\times n$单位阵，$\boldsymbol 0$为同尺寸零块；教材坐标顺序为$(\boldsymbol q,\boldsymbol p)$。
$\boldsymbol M$为固定对角质量矩阵；$\boldsymbol F(\boldsymbol q)=-\nabla U(\boldsymbol q)$为力，$\boldsymbol f$为完整相空间向量场。
extra_assumptions: 原文ODE按时间域I逐点解释；只定义关系，不宣称解存在。

audit.explanation: 重新读取Ch02.lean第18–20行及Ch02_deps.txt正式定义：SymplecticCoordinates n=(Fin n ⊕ Fin n)→ℝ（第33行），左标签为q、右标签为p；textbookJ=Matrix.fromBlocks 0 1 (-1) 0（第39–40行）；textbookHamiltonianVectorField H z=J *ᵥ (fun i => (fderiv ℝ H z)(Pi.single i 1))（第1921–1925行）。故在H可微处逐分量确为(∂H/∂p,−∂H/∂q)，梯度由标准坐标偏导组成，不是该Pi空间范数诱导的其他梯度；J符号与原书一致。量词为给定n,H,γ,I后∀t∈I要求γ在环境ℝ上有指定导数；没有解存在/唯一性结论，[EXTRA]的逐点关系解释合理。不过H完全任意，没有要求沿γ可微；fderiv在不可微点总化为零，因此可能把原书∇H根本不存在的点当作合法Hamiltonian轨道，缺少梯度存在的前提。完整原句还含固定机械模型的q̇=M⁻¹p、ṗ=−∇U；本接口未提供m,U或H与机械Hamiltonian的关联，不能单凭任意H覆盖该机械子句。采用环境HasDerivAt在开时间域上合适，若I用于闭区间端点则额外约束域外延拓，应明确约定或改用域内导数。本条没有[ERRATUM?]，无证据要求改原书；FAIL为签名与对象范围问题。此def本身无sorry；不据此评价其他依赖证明完成性，未修改或编译工程。
audit.counterexample: n=1，H(z)=|z(Sum.inl 0)|，γ(t)=0，I=ℝ。H在零点不可微，所以Lean的fderiv ℝ H 0=0，textbookHamiltonianVectorField H 0=0，常值γ满足当前hamiltonianODE。原文的∇H(0)不存在，不能把该点解释为所展示的经典Hamiltonian方程。另取H≡0及常值轨道p=1、q=0，此接口允许它，但对m=1、U=0的机械模型要求q̇=p=1。后一例说明任意H与原文指定机械H的关联不可省略，并非否定一般Hamiltonian方程。
audit.suggested_fix: 在关系中要求∀t∈I, DifferentiableAt ℝ H (γ t)，或用明确的HasFDerivAt/梯度见证表达经典向量场。保留一般Hamiltonian关系作为辅助接口，并另提供机械专用接口：显式m,U、非零或正质量、U沿配置轨道可微，以及H(z)=∑i z(inr i)^2/(2*m i)+U(q)的坐标转换关系，覆盖两条分量式。明确I为开时间域，或端点按HasDerivWithinAt解释。

audit.explanation: 重新展开Ch02.lean第24–25行及Ch02_deps.txt：CoordinateMasses n=Fin n→ℝ（第3513行），没有正性或非零约束；Position和Momentum为EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)，PhaseSpace=Position×Momentum，PotentialEnergy=Position→ℝ（第844–855行）。massHamiltonian=(massSeparableEnergy m U).hamiltonian；massSeparableEnergy=⟨momentumKineticEnergy m,U⟩；momentumKineticEnergy m p=∑i (p i)^2/(2*m i)（第3954–3961行）；SeparableEnergy.hamiltonian state=kinetic state.2+potential state.1（第3485–3486行）。因此(q,p)顺序、1/2、势能加号和固定对角质量在非零质量时准确，函数无额外量化结论。可是签名允许零质量，而原书M⁻¹需要可逆质量矩阵；库第3674–3684行也明确指出奇异矩阵逆约定不能无前提支持逐坐标倒数。缺失可逆性不仅是形式总化，在部分零质量情形还与Lean矩阵逆表达不同。[EXTRA]限制固定对角模型有第1章依据且合理，但不能补足未编码的非零质量前提。本条无[ERRATUM?]，无已确认原书错误；FAIL针对签名适用范围。此def本身没有sorry，与语义判定分开，未认证依赖证明或编译状态。
audit.counterexample: 取n=2、m=(0,1)、p=(0,1)、q=0、U≡0。展开mechanicalHamiltonian得到0²/(2*0)+1²/(2*1)=1/2（Lean零除总化）。M=diag(0,1)奇异，经典M⁻¹不存在；若按Lean Matrix的奇异逆总化为零矩阵，则pᵀM⁻¹p/2+U(q)=0，仍不等于该接口的1/2。
audit.suggested_fix: 将质量参数改为带∀i,0<m i证据的数据，或在教材专用接口显式要求∀i,m i≠0（若要求物理质量则用正性）。在该受限范围记录M=diagonalMassMatrix m并给出H(q,p)=pᵀM⁻¹p/2+U(q)对应关系。原始无约束massHamiltonian可保留为总化辅助函数，但应说明其零质量延拓不属于原文机械模型。

corrected_json.statement_latex: Suppose that the system under study has a well defined flow map $\mathscr F_t$ defined on the phase space (which is assumed to exclude any singular points of the potential energy function). The solution of the initial value problem, $\dot{\boldsymbol z}=\boldsymbol f(\boldsymbol z)$, $\boldsymbol z(0)=\boldsymbol\zeta$, may be written $\boldsymbol z(t,\boldsymbol\zeta)$ (with $\boldsymbol z(0,\boldsymbol\zeta)=\boldsymbol\zeta$), and the flow-map $\mathscr F_t$ satisfies $\mathscr F_t(\boldsymbol\zeta)=\boldsymbol z(t,\boldsymbol\zeta)$. A one-step method, starting from a given point, approximates a point on the solution trajectory at a given time $h$ units later. Such a method defines a map $\mathscr G_h$ of the phase space as illustrated in Fig. 2.1.

corrected_json.statement_latex:
Since the variation $\boldsymbol\eta$ is meant to be arbitrary, it requires
\[\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\frac{\partial L}{\partial\dot{\boldsymbol q}}(\boldsymbol q(t),\dot{\boldsymbol q}(t))=\frac{\partial L}{\partial\boldsymbol q}(\boldsymbol q(t),\dot{\boldsymbol q}(t)),\]
which is precisely the Lagrangian formulation of the equations of motion.
corrected_json.proof_note: 原书未给独立完整证明。
context_notation: PDF82／印刷60，§2.2.1：$L(\boldsymbol q,\boldsymbol v)=\boldsymbol v^T M\boldsymbol v/2-U(\boldsymbol q)$；$M$ 为质量矩阵，$U$ 在此取 $C^2$。原条选定的运动方程使用这个拉格朗日函数及其位置、速度偏导数。

PDF82／印刷60：$\boldsymbol q(t)$ 是构型空间曲线的参数化，$t\in[\alpha,\beta]$，$\boldsymbol q(\alpha)=\boldsymbol Q$、$\boldsymbol q(\beta)=\boldsymbol Q^{\prime}$；$\dot{\boldsymbol q}$ 是时间导数。该页先说 twice continuously differentiable，随后又说各分量 $C^\infty$ 及 smooth，保留这两处原文，不将其静默统一。

PDF83／印刷61，式(2.3)：$\boldsymbol q^\epsilon(t)=\boldsymbol q(t)+\epsilon\boldsymbol\eta(t)$；$\boldsymbol\eta$ 为 $C^\infty$ 曲线，$\boldsymbol\eta(\alpha)=\boldsymbol\eta(\beta)=0$。arbitrary 指满足这些资格的任意变分方向。

PDF82–84／印刷60–62：$\mathcal A_L(\Gamma)=\int_\alpha^\beta L(\boldsymbol q(t),\dot{\boldsymbol q}(t))\,dt$。本句承接 Hamilton 原理要求一阶变分为零，以及 PDF84 上方分部积分后的 $\int_\alpha^\beta [\partial L/\partial\boldsymbol q-(d/dt)(\partial L/\partial\dot{\boldsymbol q})]\boldsymbol\eta(t)\,dt=0$。

Define the variational derivative of a functional $\mathcal F$, $\delta\mathcal F/\delta\boldsymbol q$ so that
\[\mathcal F(\boldsymbol q+\epsilon\boldsymbol\eta)=\epsilon\frac{\delta\mathcal F}{\delta\boldsymbol q}\boldsymbol\eta+O(\epsilon^2),\]
for all suitable (say, $C^\infty$) functions $\boldsymbol\eta$.

context_notation: PDF84／印刷62：$\mathcal F$ 是以曲线 $\boldsymbol q$ 为自变量的泛函；$\delta\mathcal F/\delta\boldsymbol q$ 在展示式中作用于变分方向 $\boldsymbol\eta$。紧接的正文将经典作用量 $\mathcal A_L(\Gamma)$ 视作 $\mathcal F$。
PDF84／印刷62：$\epsilon$ 为变分参数，$O(\epsilon^2)$ 为 $\epsilon\to0$ 时的二阶余项；此式要求对所有 suitable (say, $C^\infty$) functions $\boldsymbol\eta$ 成立。PDF83 的作用量变分还要求零端点，但本条泛函定义的这句话未单独列出端点条件。

PDF84／印刷62 原式确为 $\mathcal F(\boldsymbol q+\epsilon\boldsymbol\eta)=\epsilon(\delta\mathcal F/\delta\boldsymbol q)\boldsymbol\eta+O(\epsilon^2)$，没有减去或加回 $\mathcal F(\boldsymbol q)$。保留印刷公式及既有 ERRATUM?，不将其替换为通常导数定义。

corrected_json.statement_latex: Any curve which satisfies this equation will represent a “stationary point” (actually, “stationary curve” would be more accurate) of the classical action. Such curves could include smooth local action minimizers, local action maximizers, or “saddle points” of the actional functional in a generalized sense. Deciding whether a given stationary curve is an actual minimizer of the action would require analysis of the second variation (the coefficient of $\epsilon^2$ in the expansion above), which introduces additional complexity.

context_notation: PDF84／印刷62，脚注4中的 this equation 承接正文紧邻展示式 $\delta\mathcal F/\delta\boldsymbol q=0$；正文称其为 stationarity condition (the Euler-Lagrange equations)，并在此取 $\mathcal F=\mathcal A_L(\Gamma)$。这里记录原文指代，不消除同页泛函导数印刷定义的 ERRATUM?。
PDF82–83／印刷60–61：经典作用量的比较对象是固定端点类 $G(\boldsymbol Q,\boldsymbol Q^{\prime};\alpha,\beta)$ 中的曲线，变分方向满足 $\boldsymbol\eta(\alpha)=\boldsymbol\eta(\beta)=0$ 并按后文取 $C^\infty$。
PDF84／印刷62，脚注4：second variation 在这段文字中指上方展开的 $\epsilon^2$ 系数；原文未在该脚注给出第二变分公式、正负定判据或严格的局部极值拓扑。PDF83 将 $C^\infty$ 称作 normed function space，但没有指定范数，不能由此补认局部极小专指一致范数。

audit.counterexample: 缺失条款本身足以判 FAIL。可作修复子命题的正质量光滑例：将 Q 1 识别为 ℝ，L(x,v)=(v²−ω²x²)/2，ω>π，q(t)=0。所有零端点 C² 方向的一阶作用量导数在0为0；η(t)=c sin(πt)，0<|c|<δ，使 action 差=c²(π²−ω²)/4<0。该例验证存在子命题可以为真，但不能补足所引三句的其他结论，也不是对该存在命题的反例。

corrected_json.statement_latex:
The first assumption is that $\mathcal G_h$ is an $O(h^{p+1})$ approximation of $\mathcal F_h$ in the sense that there is a constant $K\ge0$ and a constant $\Delta>0$ such that, for $t\in[0,\tau]$, we have
\[\|\mathcal F_h(\boldsymbol z(t))-\mathcal G_h(\boldsymbol z(t))\|\le\bar K h^{p+1},\qquad h<\Delta.\tag{2.10}\]
The assumption (2.10) that the local error is of order $p+1$, $p>0$, is termed the consistency of the numerical method. We say the method is consistent of order $p$.

Since $\dot q=p$, we have $\ddot q=\dot p=F(q)$, and the third derivative is $q^{(3)}=F'(q)p$. On the other hand $\dot p=F(q)$ implies that $\ddot p=F'(q)\dot q=pF'$, and thus
\[p^{(3)}=p^2F''+F'F.\]
The Taylor expansion of the solution is (taking $q(t)=q$, $p(t)=p$):
\[q(t+h)=q+hp+\frac{h^2}{2}F+\frac{h^3}{6}F'p+O(h^4),\]
\[p(t+h)=p+hF+\frac{h^2}{2}pF'+\frac{h^3}{6}[p^2F''+F'F]+O(h^4).\]

corrected_json.statement_latex:
To complete the convergence proof for Verlet’s method, we would still need to verify the second assumption. This requires the assumption that the force field $F$ satisfy a Lipschitz condition:
\[\|F(\boldsymbol u)-F(\boldsymbol w)\|\le\hat L\|\boldsymbol u-\boldsymbol w\|\tag{2.15}\]
for all $\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol w$. Generally speaking this could be taken to hold in a neighborhood of the solution where all approximate solutions for $h<\bar h$ are assumed to lie. With a bit of effort, it is then possible to demonstrate the stability condition for the numerical method (see Exercise 4).

context_notation: $\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol w$ 为力的输入位置；$\hat L$ 为 Lipschitz 常数，式(2.15)，印刷p.68/PDF90。
稳定性指每一步两条附近轨迹间距离至多增大因子 $1+hL$，印刷p.67/PDF89；$\bar h$ 是所有近似解仍在所述邻域内的步长阈值，印刷p.69/PDF91。

corrected_json.statement_latex:
The wedge product of the coordinate differentials $dq_i,dp_i$ may be written
\[dq_i\wedge dp_i(\boldsymbol\xi,\boldsymbol\eta)=\xi_i\eta_{i+N_c}-\xi_{i+N_c}\eta_i=\boldsymbol\xi^TJ^{(i)}\boldsymbol\eta.\]
Summing these terms results in the symplectic 2-form, denoted $\psi_S$:
\[\psi_S=\sum_{i=1}^{N_c}dq_i\wedge dp_i(\boldsymbol\xi,\boldsymbol\eta)=\boldsymbol\xi^T\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N_c}J^{(i)}\right)\boldsymbol\eta=\boldsymbol\xi^TJ\boldsymbol\eta.\]

corrected_json.proof_discussion_latex:
Computing the 2-form,
\[dQ_i\wedge dP_i=dq_i\wedge dP_i+hm_i^{-1}dP_i\wedge dP_i;\]
but $du\wedge du\equiv0$ for any $u$, hence
\[dQ_i\wedge dP_i=dq_i\wedge dP_i;\]
and (2.21) implies
\[dQ_i\wedge dP_i=dq_i\wedge dp_i-h\sum_{j=1}^{N_c}dq_i\wedge\frac{\partial^2U}{\partial q_j\partial q_i}dq_j.\]
It is then a simple exercise to show that
\[\sum_{i=1}^{N_c}\sum_{j=1}^{N_c}dq_i\wedge\frac{\partial^2U}{\partial q_j\partial q_i}dq_j=0,\]
using the skew-symmetry of the wedge product and the fact that the Hessian matrix is symmetric.

corrected_json.proof_latex:
Expand $\mathcal F_h(\boldsymbol u)$ in a Taylor series:
\[\mathcal F_h(\boldsymbol u)=\boldsymbol u+hJ
abla H+\mathcal O(h^2)=\boldsymbol u+h(J
abla H_1+J
abla H_2)+\mathcal O(h^2).\tag{2.24}\]
On the other hand,
\[\mathcal F_h^1(\boldsymbol u)=\boldsymbol u+hJ
abla H_1(\boldsymbol u)+\mathcal O(h^2),\qquad\mathcal F_h^2(\boldsymbol u)=\boldsymbol u+hJ
abla H_2(\boldsymbol u)+\mathcal O(h^2).\]
Composing the maps we have
\[\mathcal F_h^1\circ\mathcal F_h^2(\boldsymbol u)=\boldsymbol u+hJ
abla H_2(\boldsymbol u)+hJ
abla H_1(\boldsymbol u+hJ
abla H_2(\boldsymbol u))+\mathcal O(h^2).\]
Assuming $H_1$ is $C^2$, we have
\[\mathcal F_h^1\circ\mathcal F_h^2(\boldsymbol u)=\boldsymbol u+h(J
abla H_2(\boldsymbol u)+J
abla H_1(\boldsymbol u))+\mathcal O(h^2),\]
which agrees with the expansion (2.24) of the flow map through the terms of first order. Thus the splitting method does indeed provide a second order local approximation of the flow map.

corrected_json.label: Example 2.4
corrected_json.statement_latex:
Let
\[H_1(\boldsymbol q,\boldsymbol p)=\boldsymbol p^TM^{-1}\boldsymbol p/2,\qquad H_2(\boldsymbol q,\boldsymbol p)=U(\boldsymbol q),\]
then a splitting method for $H=H_1+H_2$ may be obtained by determining the flow maps for each of the two parts. For $H_1$ we have the differential equations
\[\dot{\boldsymbol q}=M^{-1}\boldsymbol p,\qquad\dot{\boldsymbol p}=\boldsymbol0.\]
The second equation tells us that $\boldsymbol p$ is constant, so it is fixed at its initial value, whereas the first equation says that $\boldsymbol q$ evolves on a linear path, hence its flow map is
\[\boldsymbol Q=\boldsymbol q+hM^{-1}\boldsymbol p,\qquad\boldsymbol P=\boldsymbol p.\]

corrected_json.label: Example 2.5 (Verlet is Symplectic)
corrected_json.statement_latex:
For the Symplectic Euler method $\mathcal G_h$ and its adjoint method $\mathcal G_h^\dagger$, consider the composition
\[\mathcal K_h:=\mathcal G_{h/2}^\dagger\circ\mathcal G_{h/2}.\]
corrected_json.proof_latex:
Let
\[\begin{bmatrix}\bar{\boldsymbol q}\\\bar{\boldsymbol p}\end{bmatrix}=\mathcal G_{h/2}\begin{bmatrix}\boldsymbol q\\\boldsymbol p\end{bmatrix},\]
i.e.,
\[\bar{\boldsymbol q}=\boldsymbol q+(h/2)M^{-1}\bar{\boldsymbol p},\qquad\bar{\boldsymbol p}=\boldsymbol p-(h/2)
abla U(\boldsymbol q).\]
and set
\[\begin{bmatrix}\boldsymbol Q\\\boldsymbol P\end{bmatrix}=\mathcal G_{h/2}^\dagger\begin{bmatrix}\bar{\boldsymbol q}\\\bar{\boldsymbol p}\end{bmatrix},\]
i.e.,
\[\boldsymbol Q=\bar{\boldsymbol q}+(h/2)M^{-1}\bar{\boldsymbol p},\qquad\boldsymbol P=\bar{\boldsymbol p}-(h/2)
abla U(\boldsymbol Q).\]
The composition simplifies to
\[\bar{\boldsymbol p}=\boldsymbol p-\frac h2
abla U(\boldsymbol q),\qquad\boldsymbol Q=\boldsymbol q+hM^{-1}\bar{\boldsymbol p},\qquad\boldsymbol P=\bar{\boldsymbol p}-\frac h2
abla U(\boldsymbol Q).\]
This is just the leapfrog/Verlet method in its Hamiltonian form.

corrected_json.statement_latex:
Some systems can be decomposed into a harmonic (quadratic) part $H_0(\boldsymbol q,\boldsymbol p)=\boldsymbol p^T M^{-1}\boldsymbol p/2+\boldsymbol q^T A\boldsymbol q/2$ and an anharmonic part $H_1(\boldsymbol q,\boldsymbol p)=\hat U(\boldsymbol q)$. Then a splitting method can be formulated based on exact solution of the linear system together with “kicks” representing impulses defined by the anharmonic part. For a simple system consisting of a harmonic oscillator $H_0(q,p)=p^2/2+\Omega^2q^2/2$, such a method can be written
\[\begin{bmatrix}Q\\\hat p\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\cos h\Omega&\frac{1}{\Omega}\sin h\Omega\\-\Omega\sin h\Omega&\cos h\Omega\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}q\\p\end{bmatrix},\qquad P=\hat p-h\hat U'(Q).\]

corrected_json.statement_latex:
An implicit method will typically result in a system of nonlinear equations of the form
\[g(\boldsymbol z_{n+1})=\boldsymbol\tau_n,\tag{2.25}\]
which will need to be solved at each timestep. The right hand side $\boldsymbol\tau_n$ is a vector that depends on the previous time-step $\boldsymbol z_n$, perhaps in a complicated way. We may assume the number of equations represented by (2.25) is equal to the dimension of the space where $\boldsymbol z$ is defined, so we have a square nonlinear system. Typically $g$ will depend on the stepsize and coefficients of the method and will have the property that for $h$ sufficiently small, the solution is uniquely defined and is continuously defined in terms of $\boldsymbol\tau_n$, that is the mapping $g$ has a bounded and smooth inverse.

corrected_json.statement_latex:
The Backward Euler method,
\[\boldsymbol z_{n+1}=\boldsymbol z_n+hf(\boldsymbol z_{n+1}),\]
is an example of an implicit method. The calculation of a timestep involves solving a system of equations of the form
\[g(\boldsymbol w)\equiv\boldsymbol w-\boldsymbol z_n-hf(\boldsymbol w)=\boldsymbol0.\]
The map $\mathcal G_t$ is defined implicitly by the equation
\[\mathcal G_h(\boldsymbol z)=\boldsymbol z+hf(\mathcal G_h(\boldsymbol z)).\]

Solving the system may then proceed, from an initial guess $\boldsymbol z_{n+1}^{(0)}$ by use of Newton’s method:
\[\boldsymbol z_{n+1}^{(k+1)}=\boldsymbol z_{n+1}^{(k)}-[J^{(k)}]^{-1}(g(\boldsymbol z_n^{(k)})-\boldsymbol\tau_n),\]
where $J^{(k)}$ is the Jacobian matrix of the mapping $g$ evaluated at $\boldsymbol z_n^{(k)}$, or else an approximation of this Jacobian (assumed to be nonsingular due to the invertibility of the mapping). The iteration may be recast in the form
\[\boldsymbol b_k=-(g(\boldsymbol z_n^{(k)})-\boldsymbol\tau_n),\quad J^{(k)}\Delta\boldsymbol z_k=\boldsymbol b_k,\quad\boldsymbol z_{n+1}^{(k+1)}=\boldsymbol z_{n+1}^{(k)}+\Delta\boldsymbol z_k.\]

Let us suppose that we have such a conjugacy between two numerical methods $\mathcal G_h$ and $\tilde{\mathcal G}_h$, that is
\[\mathcal G_h=\chi_h^{-1}\circ\tilde{\mathcal G}_h\circ\chi_h,\]
defined in such a way that $\mathcal G_h$ has order $r$ and $\tilde{\mathcal G}_h$ has order $s$ where $s<r$. Then, given an initial condition $\boldsymbol z_0$, we first modify (“pre-process”) this to $\tilde{\boldsymbol z}_0=\chi_h(\boldsymbol z_0)$, then take multiple steps with the method $\tilde{\mathcal G}_h$, and finally transform (“post-process”) the end result by $\chi_h^{-1}$.

corrected_json.statement_latex:
To see that it is symplectic, we first note that this is a symmetric composition of the form
\[\mathcal K_h=\mathcal G_{h/2}^{\dagger}\circ\mathcal G_{h/2},\]
so it is enough to show that this basic method is symplectic.
corrected_json.proof_latex:
Taking differentials of (2.30) defining $\mathcal G_h$ and then wedge products and summing, we have
\[\sum_i dQ_i\wedge dP_i=\sum_i dq_i\wedge dP_i+h\sum_i\sum_j H_{p_iq_j}dq_j\wedge dP_i+h\sum_i\sum_j H_{p_ip_j}dP_j\wedge dP_i.\]
The last term on the right vanishes by equality of mixed partials and the antisymmetry of the wedge product. On the other hand, using (2.29), we obtain, by similar means,
\[\sum_i dq_i\wedge dP_i=\sum_i dq_i\wedge dp_i-h\sum_i\sum_j H_{q_ip_j}dq_i\wedge dP_j.\]
Relabelling the indices in the sum and using our previous work results in
\[\sum_i dQ_i\wedge dP_i=\sum_i dq_i\wedge dp_i,\]
implying that the method is symplectic.
